overview.summary: Chapter 1: Field Visit. Questions and source-provided answers from the supplied Geography PDF are grouped here by chapter. Map exercises are omitted; graph questions and available data are retained.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 6: Arrange the Sentences
notes.content:
Q. Preparing for field visit :                                    (July ’19)

(A) Visit to a location of field visit.

(B) Selection of a place for field visit.

(C) Report writing

(D) Pre-preparation for a field visit

Options : (i) (B), (D), (A), (C)       (ii) (C), (A), (B), (D) (iii) (D), (A), (B), (C)   (iv) (A), (B), (C), (D)

Ans. Statements in correct sequence – (i) (B), (D), (A), (C).

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 9: Answer in One Sentence
notes.content:
(1) What is field visit?

Ans. Collecting geographical and cultural information by actually paying a visit to a particular place is called ‘field visit’.

(2) What types of information of a field can be collected by field visit?

Ans. Geographical, social, economic, historical, cultural, etc. types of information of a field can be collected by field visit.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 11: Say Right or Wrong
notes.content:
(1) During field visit, vegetation is not the indicator of difference in precipitation.                                   (March ’19)

(2) During field visit, the information can be obtained by interviewing local people.

(3) Regions and necessities influence the difference in the means of livelihood.

(4) Vegetation is an indicator of difference in precipitation.

Ans. (1) Wrong (2) Right (3) Right (4) Right.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 14: Write Short Notes
notes.content:
(1) Items to be carried for a field visit.        (March ’23)

Ans. The items to carry are: a notebook, pen, pencil, scale and camera; a compass and maps; a purpose-specific questionnaire; containers or bags for samples; a cap, drinking water and a first-aid box.

(2) Precautions to be taken continuously during field visit.

Ans. We will take the following precautions continuously during field visit :

(1) We will ensure safety of oneself and others and will carry identity card, first aid box, etc. with oneself for emergency circumstances.

(2) We will strictly obey the instructions given by teachers.

(3) During field visit, we will try to gather information about local circumstances by conversing with the local people.

(4) We will also ensure that one does not harm the environment in any way during field visit.

notes.title: 2026 Question Set 20: Answer in Detail / Explain
notes.content:
(1) What is field visit? What are the things you carry for field visit?                                                 (Sept. ’21)

Ans. (A) Meaning : A field visit is the study, by observation, of the natural and cultural features of a selected small area; studying the entire Earth in a field visit is not possible.

(B) The items to carry are a notebook, pen, pencil, scale and camera; a compass and maps; a purpose-specific questionnaire; containers or bags for samples; a cap, drinking water and a first-aid box.

(2) How will you manage the litter during field visit? (March ’19; July ’23)

Ans. We will manage the litter during the field visit in the following ways :

(1) Carrying containers/bags/dustbins to collect litter dumped on a field.

(2) Informing everyone to not to dump trash/waste on a field during field visit.

(3) Creating awareness about cleanliness using charts and banners or performing street play, etc.

(4) Informing and requesting officials of local corporations for taking immediate remedial actions against litter/waste dump on a field.

(3) Prepare a questionnaire for a field visit to a sugar factory/ factory.                                     (Nov. ’20; March ’24)

Ans. The questionnaire for a field visit to a sugar factory/factory is as follows :

(1) What is the year of establishment of this factory?

(2) Which goods are manufactured in this factory?

(3) How many workers are working in this factory?

(4) Which raw material is essential for the goods manufactured in this factory?

(5) From where is the raw material required for manufacturing the goods purchased?

(6) Where are the goods manufactured supplied?

(7) Which precautionary measures are taken to ensure the safety of workers?

(8) Which environment protecting measures are taken by this factory?

(4) (A) What items will you take with you for the field visit?

(B) What care will you take when you visit a seashore? (July ’19)

Ans. (A) The items to be taken for the field visit : (1) Notebook, pen, pencil, scale, camera, etc. to collect information.

(2) Compass for knowing directions and maps for understanding various locations.

(3) Questionnaire as per the purpose of field visit.

(4) Containers or bags for collecting samples of water/soil/rocks/ plants/crops, etc. Also a cap, a bottle of drinking water, first aid box, etc.

(B) We will take care of the following when we visit a seashore : At the seashore, check high- and low-tide times; use a local guide and avoid unknown places; do not take selfies near cliffs or deep water; do not swim in deep water; keep the shore clean; and follow teachers’ and posted instructions.

(5) If you are a part of field visit, what preparations will you make?                                                            OR Suppose teachers ask you to plan the visit, how will you plan the details of the trip?

Ans. We will make the following preparations/plan the following details of the trip :

(1) Deciding the place : (1) It includes planning about the location, distance, transportation route, means of transportation, duration of field visit, etc. (2) For example, deciding a place like

river bank/seashore/mountain/fort/plateau/farm/hill station/factory/ railway station, etc.

(2) Deciding the purpose : (1) It includes deciding the aims and learning objectives of field visit. (2) For example, visiting a hill station and seashore to study the differences in climatic conditions between them.

(3) Collecting/Obtaining essential documents : (1) It includes collecting or obtaining the location map of a field, necessary permission letters, etc. (2) For example, obtaining permission letter of owner of a factory allowing a visit to a factory.

(4) Preparing     questionnaire : (1) It     includes    preparing questionnaire as per the purpose of field visit. (2) For example, preparing following type of questionnaire to gather information from a farmer working on a farm : (i) For which crops is this land suitable? (ii) Which precautions are taken to protect crops from any harm? (iii) What type of irrigation is used for growing crops?

(6) What is field visit? What preparations should be done before going to a field visit?                    (March ’25)

Ans. (A) Meaning : A field visit is the study, by observation, of the natural and cultural features of a selected small area; studying the entire Earth in a field visit is not possible.

(B) Decide the place, route, transport and duration; set the learning objectives; obtain required location information and permission; and prepare a questionnaire suited to the visit.

notes.title: July 2024 Solved Paper, Assignment and July 2025 Practice Paper
notes.content:
July 2024 Board Paper — Q.1: Visiting a given place and gaining first-hand information is known as which activity? Options: Field visit; health tourism; census; house visit.

Ans. Field visit.

Q.7(1): What is a field visit? What precautions would you take when visiting a seacoast?

Ans. A field visit is the study of natural and cultural features of a selected small area by observation. At the seashore: confirm high- and low-tide times; take a local guide and avoid unknown places; avoid selfies near sea cliffs or deep water; do not swim in deep water; keep the shore clean; and follow teachers’ and posted instructions.

Assignment — Q.7(A): What preparations would you make before a field visit? Prepare a questionnaire for a forest visit. Q.7(B): Prepare a questionnaire for interviewing a farmer during a field visit.

Assignment answers are not printed in the supplied PDF; it refers to a separate Geography Digest.

July 2025 Practice Board Paper — Q.2 matching item: Field Visit. The PDF’s matching choices include “Questionnaire.” Q.7(1): What preparations would you make before a field visit? Prepare a questionnaire for visiting a weather station.

The July 2025 answers are not printed in the supplied PDF; it points to a QR code for model answers.

quiz.question: What is a field visit?
options: Collecting geographical information from the internet.
Collecting geographical and cultural information by actually paying a visit to a particular place.
Studying maps and diagrams in a classroom.
Writing a report based on a textbook.
quiz.explanation: A field visit involves directly visiting a place to collect geographical and cultural information first-hand.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT an essential material for a field visit?
quiz.explanation:
A bar chart is a method of presenting data and is not an essential item to carry on a field visit itself.
Items like a notebook, map, and camera are directly useful for collection and observation.

quiz.question: What should you carry for a field visit to collect information?
quiz.explanation: A questionnaire is prepared beforehand to guide the collection of specific information from the field.

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT a main purpose of a field visit?
quiz.explanation:
The main purposes are geographical, historical, cultural, and social studies.
Entertainment is not the primary objective.
